Early production batches suffered from guidance and manufacturing flaws, resulting in a reported circular error probable (CEP) of around 800–1,000 meters, and in some cases even missing targets by several kilometers. By comparison, Russia's Iskander-M has a CEP of about 5–10 meters. Following its poor performance, North Korea reportedly introduced a series of upgrades to the Hwasongpho-11Ga. headline: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) has issued a fact check in response to renewed Iranian claims that the Strait of Hormuz has been closed, stating that the claim is false. According to CENTCOM, commercial shipping continues to transit the waterway, which remains open despite the ongoing conflict. The command noted that Iran does not control the entire strait and that thousands of commercial vessels have successfully transited since the war began. Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz averaged approximately 130 commercial vessel transits per day. Since February 28, roughly 19,900 transits would have been expected under normal conditions. Instead, daily traffic has generally remained at around 10% of pre-war levels, with only occasional surges. The majority of commercial traffic has continued to use Iran's designated shipping channel, while an unknown number of vessels have instead transited via the U.S. established maritime safety corridor through Omani waters. Several vessels using that route have subsequently come under Iranian attack, underscoring that while the strait remains open, commercial shipping continues to operate in a high-threat environment.

headline: The Washington Post reports that U.S. intelligence agencies have assessed Iran was likely behind a coordinated cyberattack targeting more than 30 municipal water systems in Minnesota, though officials say the assessment is not yet definitive and the FBI's investigation remains ongoing. According to the Post, the attack disrupted control systems at multiple water facilities but did not contaminate drinking water or cause widespread service outages. The report notes federal cybersecurity officials have warned for months that Iranian cyber actors have been targeting internet-connected industrial control systems used by U.S. water, wastewater, and energy facilities. Previous Iranian linked cyber activity has targeted water infrastructure, including incidents involving Pennsylvania utilities and repeated CISA warnings about Iranian exploitation of programmable logic controllers (PLCs), but those cases were narrower in scope or attributed after law enforcement investigations rather than through a contemporaneous intelligence assessment. Source: https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/07/30/us-spy-agencies-suspect-iran-launched-cyberattack-minnesota-water-facilities/

headline: President Donald J. Trump announced that the Board of Peace has reached what he described as a "historic" agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza. The Board of Peace is a U.S.-led international organization established earlier this year to oversee post-conflict stabilization, reconstruction, and governance in Gaza under Trump's broader peace plan. According to Trump, the agreement will be implemented in phases, with Hamas disarming, Israeli forces withdrawing as benchmarks are met, and an International Stabilization Force working alongside a new Palestinian police force under a new Palestinian government. Trump also credited Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey for their mediation efforts, calling the agreement a major milestone in his 20-Point Plan and stating that Gaza "will no longer be used as a base for terror attacks." Current Board of Peace members include: United States, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Qatar, United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, Morocco, Kuwait, Pakistan, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Mongolia, Vietnam, Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Hungary, Kosovo, Argentina, and Paraguay.
